data.name: Austria
data.summary: Austria taxes a resident's capital gains on securities and dividends at a flat 27.5% (bank interest 25%) regardless of holding period or size of holding, and real estate gains at 30%. There is no wealth tax and no inheritance or gift tax (abolished 2008), so children inherit a securities portfolio tax-free; only real estate passing within the family bears a stepped real estate transfer tax of 0.5%-3.5% plus a 1.1% registration fee, and larger lifetime gifts must be notified to the tax office. Emigration triggers a deemed sale of financial assets, deferred without interest for moves within the EU/EEA.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Unlimited liability on worldwide income for residents. Investment income is taxed at special flat rates (§ 27a EStG) that are final when withheld by an Austrian bank.
regimes.eligibility: A home (Wohnsitz) in Austria or habitual abode (stay of more than six months). Non-EU citizens need a residence permit.

capital_gains.summary: Gains on shares, bonds, funds and derivatives are taxed at a flat 27.5% (§ 27a(1) EStG) whatever the holding period and whatever the size of the shareholding, including substantial private-company stakes. Gains on private real estate are taxed at a flat 30% (§ 30a EStG); the main residence is exempt under conditions. There is no annual allowance.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: No allowance for capital income. Main residence exempt if lived in for 2 years since acquisition or 5 of the last 10 years. Shares bought before 2011 (bonds/derivatives before 30 March 2012) are grandfathered and tax-free, unless a holding of at least 1%.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Resident individual holding as private assets. Austrian banks withhold the 27.5% as a final tax; foreign accounts are declared in the return at the same rate. Option to be taxed at the regular progressive rate if lower (Regelbesteuerungsoption).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Losses can be offset only within the same year against other capital income (not against bank interest), and cannot be carried forward. Exit tax (§ 27(6) Z 1 EStG): leaving Austria is a deemed sale of all financial assets at market value; for a move to an EU/EEA state the tax is assessed but not collected until actual sale (annual proof required if relevant income exceeds EUR 100,000); a move outside the EU/EEA makes the tax due. Since 1 January 2025 a 30% surcharge applies to gains from land rezoned to building land.

open_questions: Main-residence exemption conditions and the 2025 rezoning surcharge were taken from general knowledge and a Deloitte search summary; the § 30 EStG text was not opened.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Securities and private business shares: the 27.5% special rate of § 27a(1) Z 2 EStG applies to all capital gains of private investors, with no surcharges and no holding-period relief. Real estate: 30% flat under § 30a(1) EStG. Foreign real estate: the 30% Austrian rate before treaty relief; most Austrian treaties leave real estate gains to the situs country (Austria then exempts or credits).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Low risk for securities: capital income of private investors stays under § 27 even with frequent trading. Commercial real estate dealing can turn real estate gains into business income at progressive rates (up to 55%).
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: None for securities acquired after 2010 (bonds/derivatives after 30 March 2012) or for real estate.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide taxation at the same rates; foreign accounts declared in the return. Foreign real estate gains depend on the treaty with the situs country.

dividends.summary: Dividends, domestic or foreign, are taxed at a flat 27.5%, withheld as a final tax by Austrian banks or declared in the return for foreign accounts. Foreign withholding tax is credited up to 15% via the Austrian custodian bank, regardless of the treaty.
dividends.eligibility_conditions: Private shareholder; option for progressive taxation if lower.
dividends.important_exceptions: Foreign withholding above 15% must be reclaimed from the source country.

dividends.rate_basis: 27.5% special rate (§ 27a(1) Z 2 EStG); foreign dividends taxed at 27.5% of the gross amount with a credit for foreign withholding tax of at most 15%.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 27.5% KESt on dividends paid to individuals; 23% to corporations; reduced by treaties and to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
dividends.treaty_network: About 90 income tax treaties including the US and all EU states.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Two structures are modelled as their own regimes. Privatstiftung (private foundation): from 2026 it pays 27.5% interim tax (Zwischensteuer, § 22(2) KStG) on realised gains, interest, derivatives and private real estate sales (§ 13(3) KStG), but dividends from foreign companies that are comparable to an Austrian corporation and resident in a state with comprehensive administrative assistance, and domestic dividends, are exempt (§ 13(2) with § 10(1) Z 1, 5-7 KStG); distributions (Zuwendungen) bear 27.5% KESt, and distributions in excess of the year's separately taxed income earn a credit of the interim tax (§ 24(5) KStG); the endowment bears 3.5% foundation entry tax from 1 January 2026. Asset-management GmbH: 23% corporate tax on realised gains (24% above EUR 1,000,000 of income from 2028), portfolio dividends exempt under § 10 KStG, and 27.5% KESt when it distributes. Austria has no inheritance tax to avoid, so neither structure saves tax at death.

wealth_tax.summary: Austria has no wealth tax (net wealth tax not levied since 1994).
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: Reintroducing wealth and inheritance taxes is a recurring SPÖ demand; the 2025 coalition (ÖVP-SPÖ-NEOS) budget measures did not include one.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal Grundsteuer based on the old assessed value (Einheitswert), at most 1% of assessed value; usually small.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance or gift tax since 1 August 2008. A securities portfolio passes to children tax-free. Real estate passing within the family bears real estate transfer tax on the property value at stepped rates (0.5% on the first EUR 250,000, 2% on the next EUR 150,000, 3.5% above), plus a 1.1% land-registry fee. Lifetime gifts of cash, securities and company shares above EUR 50,000 a year between relatives must be notified within three months (fine up to 10% of value if deliberately not reported).
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Gift notification duty (§ 121a BAO): gifts between relatives up to EUR 50,000 per donor and recipient in one year are exempt from notification; real estate is notified under the real estate transfer tax act instead.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Transfers to a private foundation bear 3.5% foundation entry tax (Stiftungseingangssteuer; 2.5% until 31 December 2025, raised from 1 January 2026 by the Budgetbegleitgesetz 2025). Inherited real estate: real estate transfer tax (stepped, family rates, aggregated over 5 years) plus 1.1% registration fee on the property value (Grundstückswert). Political proposals to reintroduce inheritance tax are not enacted.

inheritance.domicile_rules: Not relevant; there is no inheritance tax. The gift notification duty applies if donor or recipient lives in Austria.

regimes.name: Private foundation (Privatstiftung, PSG)
regimes.description: The family endows an Austrian Privatstiftung with the portfolio. The foundation is its own legal person (§ 1 PSG) and owns the portfolio. It pays no tax on foreign portfolio dividends (exempt under § 13(2) and § 10(1) KStG) but 27.5% interim tax (Zwischensteuer) on realised gains, interest and derivatives (§ 13(3), § 22(2) KStG, rate from 2026). Distributions to beneficiaries (Zuwendungen) bear 27.5% KESt, and the interim tax is credited when distributions exceed the separately taxed income (§ 24(5) KStG). Endowing it costs 3.5% foundation entry tax. Austria has no inheritance tax, so the foundation offers no estate-tax saving; its use is control, succession planning and deferral of tax on dividends.
regimes.eligibility: Any person can found a Privatstiftung with assets of at least EUR 70,000 (§ 4 PSG); it must have its seat in Austria and a board of at least three members, two of them habitually resident in the EU/EEA (§ 1, § 15 PSG). Founded by notarial deed and entered in the commercial register.
regimes.duration_note: A foundation under ordinary law with no time limit; it ends only on dissolution under its deed (§ 34 PSG covers revocation, possible only if the founder reserved it).

structure.entity: Privatstiftung (Austrian private foundation under the PSG)
structure.payout_notes: Zuwendungen of any kind from a Privatstiftung are capital income of the beneficiary (§ 27(5) Z 7 EStG), taxed at 27.5% KESt (§ 27a(1) Z 2 EStG), withheld by the foundation when paid. The foundation's interim tax is reduced or credited when Zuwendungen are made: its separately taxed base is cut by Zuwendungen on which KESt was withheld (§ 13(3) KStG) and the excess of Zuwendungen over that base earns a credit at 27.5% (§ 24(5) Z 3-4 KStG, years from 2026).
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: The board needs at least three members, two habitually resident in the EU/EEA (§ 15 PSG); a court-appointed foundation auditor reviews the annual accounts (§ 20 PSG); minimum endowment EUR 70,000 (§ 4 PSG). Entry tax: 3.5% of the endowed assets from 1 January 2026 (2.5% before); a 25% rate applies where the foundation is not comparable to a Privatstiftung or required documents are not filed (law-firm summaries); real estate bears the real estate transfer tax equivalent instead. The exemption for foreign dividends needs a comparable foreign corporation in a state with comprehensive administrative assistance (§ 10(1) Z 6 KStG), and is denied where the payer can deduct the dividend (§ 10(4) KStG); fund distributions are not covered. Realised gains on holdings of at least 1% in the last five years can be rolled over (§ 13(4) KStG), not relevant for a diversified portfolio.
structure.exit_and_liquidation: On dissolution the remaining assets pass to the final beneficiary named in the deed (the founder, if the deed is silent, § 34 PSG) and are taxed as Zuwendungen at 27.5% (§ 27(5) Z 7 EStG; treatment of the endowed capital not verified). The founder's death changes nothing: the assets belong to the foundation.

Unrealised gains are not taxed. Losses can be offset only against other capital income of the same year (§ 27(8) EStG applies, Brandauer).
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: None for the foundation. Distributions in the year reduce the separately taxed base and, where they exceed it, earn a credit of 27.5% (§ 13(3), § 24(5) KStG).
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Privatstiftung under the PSG, not a foundation exempt under § 5 Z 6 KStG (charitable).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Shareholdings of at least 1% in the last five years: the hidden reserves can be rolled over into a new holding above 10% or set aside as a tax-free amount for 12 months (§ 13(4) KStG). An international participation of at least 10% held a year is tax-neutral (§ 10(2)-(3) KStG), not relevant for a portfolio of small positions.

dividends.summary: Dividends are exempt at the foundation: domestic dividends under § 10(1) Z 1 KStG, and foreign dividends under § 13(2) KStG with § 10(1) Z 5-7 (EU parent-subsidiary companies, comparable corporations in states with comprehensive administrative assistance, international participations). They are not among the income taxed by Zwischensteuer (§ 13(3) KStG lists interest, gains, derivatives, crypto and private real estate only). Foreign withholding tax is therefore not credited and is a final cost; the dividend only becomes taxable (27.5% KESt) when the foundation distributes it.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: No minimum stake for the Z 5/Z 6 exemptions.
dividends.eligibility_conditions: Payer must be comparable to an Austrian corporation and resident in the EU/EEA or a state with comprehensive administrative assistance; exemption is denied if the dividend is deductible at the payer (§ 10(4) KStG).
dividends.important_exceptions: Fund distributions, dividends from companies in states without comprehensive administrative assistance and deductible payments are not exempt; they were not modelled.

regimes.name: Asset-management GmbH (vermögensverwaltende GmbH)
regimes.description: The family holds the portfolio through an Austrian GmbH. The GmbH pays 23% corporate tax on realised share gains (no exemption for stakes below 10%) but portfolio dividends from comparable foreign corporations in states with comprehensive administrative assistance, and domestic dividends, are exempt (§ 10 KStG). Distributions to the family bear 27.5% KESt. Austria has no inheritance tax, so the GmbH offers no estate-tax saving; its use is deferral of the personal 27.5% tax on dividends and gains.
regimes.eligibility: Any resident can found a GmbH by notarial deed and entry in the commercial register. The shares are private assets of the family.
regimes.duration_note: A company under ordinary law with no time limit; from 2028 the corporate tax rises to 24% on income above EUR 1,000,000 a year (§ 22(1) KStG as amended by BGBl. I Nr. 62/2026).

structure.payout_notes: Distributions to individuals are dividends: 27.5% KESt withheld by the GmbH (PwC; § 27a(1) Z 2 EStG). Repayments of contributed capital and shareholder loans are not modelled.
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: Corporate tax of at least EUR 500 a year is due even in a loss year (minimum tax EUR 125 per quarter since 2024, § 24(4) KStG), creditable against later tax. Exemption of foreign portfolio dividends needs a comparable corporation in a state with comprehensive administrative assistance and no deductibility at the payer (§ 10(1) Z 6, (4) KStG). An international participation (at least 10% for a year) is tax-neutral on gains and dividends (§ 10(2)-(3) KStG), which a diversified portfolio of small positions does not reach. Relief for foreign withholding is by credit capped at Austrian tax on that income, which is nil on exempt dividends, with no carry-forward (PwC).
structure.exit_and_liquidation: Liquidation proceeds were not researched. Death of a shareholder: the shares pass to the heirs without Austrian inheritance tax and without a deemed sale (Austria has no inheritance tax; whether the heirs carry over the shares' acquisition cost was not researched).

income_tax.summary: Austria taxes residents on worldwide income with seven brackets for 2026: 0% to EUR 13,539, then 20%, 30%, 40%, 48%, 50% above EUR 104,859 and 55% above EUR 1 million. There is no municipal income tax in Vienna. Employees pay 18.07% social insurance up to a monthly ceiling of EUR 6,930; the self-employed (GSVG) pay 18.5% pension, 6.8% health and 1.53% self-employed provision on income up to EUR 8,085 a month.

Monthly maximum base EUR 8,085 (EUR 97,020 a year, contributions max EUR 2,182.17 a month); minimum base EUR 551.10 a month. Contributions are provisional until the final tax assessment. Free professions have different schemes.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income tax. Employee rate 18.07% = sickness 3.87 + unemployment 2.95 + pension 10.25 + miscellaneous 1.00 on the monthly ceiling EUR 6,930 (EUR 13,860 more on special payments, taxed at 17.07%). The 13th and 14th salary are taxed at 6% above an EUR 620 exemption (rates 6% to 55%), not at the scale above. Brackets are the PwC 2026 table.

open_questions: Official 2026 Rot-Weiß-Rot Card and Blue Card salary minima not verified.
No source for a 2-bedroom rent in Vienna.

succession.name: Austria
succession.summary: Children and the spouse are guaranteed half of their intestate share (Pflichtteil), and a will cannot remove it. A foreign national habitually resident in Austria can choose the law of their nationality under the EU Succession Regulation. Austria has no trust law, but a Privatstiftung (private foundation) can be set up under the PSG.
succession.reserved_share: Descendants and spouse or registered partner: a Pflichtteil of half their statutory share, paid in money (ABGB sections 756-759; parents and other ascendants no longer protected since the 2017 reform).
succession.foreign_law_note: Reg. 650/2012 art. 22 lets a person choose the law of their nationality for the whole estate; without a choice, the law of last habitual residence applies (art. 21). A choice of foreign law removes the Austrian Pflichtteil, subject to the public-policy exception (art. 35).
succession.trust_note: Austria has no domestic trust law and is not party to the Hague Trusts Convention. The HCCH status table lists no signature or ratification for this state; the Convention is not in force here. Foreign trusts are treated in practice as contractual or fiduciary arrangements. Transfers to a Privatstiftung (Privatstiftungsgesetz 1993) are taxed under the Stiftungseingangssteuergesetz, which also reaches comparable foreign foundations.
open_questions: Austrian tax treatment of foreign trusts (Stiftungseingangssteuergesetz scope, income tax on distributions) was not examined in detail.
Exact ABGB section numbers for the 2017 Pflichtteil rules were taken from memory plus general guides and should be checked at ris.bka.gv.at.

assumptions: Austrian tax rates on investment income are flat (27.5%), so the 'top marginal rates' assumption has no effect on the checks.

Foreign dividends are assumed to come from companies resident in the EU/EEA or in states with comprehensive administrative assistance and comparable to an Austrian corporation (the § 10(1) Z 5-7 KStG exemption for the foundation and the GmbH); fund distributions are not covered.
The Privatstiftung and the GmbH hold the portfolio in positions below 10% of each company; the 1% and 10% rules of § 13(4) and § 10(2) KStG do not apply.
Running costs of the foundation and the GmbH are not in the tax file: no sourced euro amount for the board, auditor or accountant was found, so both structures are slightly flattered.
The family home is held personally under every path.
open_questions: Needs an engine change: the Privatstiftung's interim tax is reduced or credited when it makes distributions. Its separately taxed base is cut by Zuwendungen on which KESt was withheld (§ 13(3) last sentence KStG) and the excess of Zuwendungen over the base earns a credit of 27.5% (§ 24(5) Z 3-4 KStG, years from 2026). The engine charges 27.5% on all realised gains and then 27.5% on the payout, so it overstates the foundation's tax whenever the family takes out at least the year's gains.

Needs an engine change: the endowment of a Privatstiftung bears a one-off 3.5% foundation entry tax (§ 2 StiftEG as amended by the Budgetbegleitgesetz 2025, from 1 January 2026), about EUR 1,050,000 on EUR 30,000,000. The engine has no one-off entry cost on moving the portfolio into a structure.

Needs an engine change: from 2028 the corporate tax rate is 23%, rising to 24% on income above EUR 1,000,000 a year (§ 22(1) KStG as amended by BGBl. I Nr. 62/2026). The engine takes one rate (23%), so the GmbH is undertaxed once its nominal income passes EUR 1,000,000 (roughly from year 30 if the realised gains, 1.5% of a portfolio that keeps its real value, grow with 2.5% inflation).

Needs an engine change: inherited Austrian real estate bears real estate transfer tax at 0.5% (first EUR 250,000), 2% (next EUR 150,000) and 3.5% (above) plus a 1.1% registration fee, per the tax file (PwC confirms the stepped rates for non-remunerated transfers). The engine's other_transfer_cost_rate is a share of the whole estate, so it cannot charge the home alone; it is left at 0 and the two deaths omit this cost.

Running costs of a Privatstiftung (at least three board members, foundation auditor, accounts) and of a GmbH are not in the tax file; law-firm pages say only 'five-figure range' a year. Find a sourced fee schedule (for example from a Wirtschaftstreuhänder or a foundation association) before relying on the comparison.
The foundation entry tax and the consolidated StiftEG text were not opened on RIS; the 3.5% rate rests on the government bill's explanatory note and two law-firm summaries.

A family trust is not an Austrian vehicle (no Austrian trust law was found; not researched further). § 27(5) Z 7 EStG treats distributions of comparable foreign foundations or asset pools like Privatstiftung Zuwendungen. Not modelled.

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally
paths.note: Dividends and realised gains are taxed at the flat 27.5% special rate (§ 27a(1) Z 2 EStG) whatever the holding period; foreign withholding tax is credited up to 15% (PwC). There is no wealth tax and no inheritance or gift tax, so the portfolio passes to the children untaxed. No special regime applies: the § 103 EStG immigration relief is for scientists, artists and athletes in the public interest and the family has no such activity.

paths.name: Private foundation (Privatstiftung)
paths.note: The Privatstiftung is its own legal person that owns the endowed assets (§ 1 PSG), so nothing of the portfolio passes at the founder's death (Austria has no inheritance tax in any case). It pays no tax on portfolio dividends (§ 13(2), § 10(1) KStG) and 27.5% interim tax on realised gains (§ 13(3), § 22(2) KStG, from 2026); beneficiaries pay 27.5% KESt on distributions (§ 27(5) Z 7 EStG), and the interim tax is credited when distributions exceed the year's separately taxed income (§ 24(5) KStG). The endowment bears 3.5% foundation entry tax. Running costs (three-member board, foundation auditor) are not in the tax file: no sourced euro figure was found.

paths.name: Asset-management GmbH
paths.note: A GmbH owned by the parents pays 23% corporate tax on realised gains (no exemption below 10%) and nothing on portfolio dividends (§ 10 KStG); distributions bear 27.5% KESt. The shares are in the estate, where Austria levies no inheritance tax. Running costs are not in the tax file.

immigration.name: Austria
immigration.summary: EU citizens register and get an Anmeldebescheinigung after three months. Austria has no golden visa. Non-EU people of independent means can apply for a Niederlassungsbewilligung - ausgenommen Erwerbstaetigkeit (the 'Privatier' permit): it needs a free place in a small annual quota (385 in 2025) and monthly income of twice the pension compensation rate (twice EUR 1,308.39 in 2026). Citizenship for 'extraordinary merit' (Section 10(6)) is discretionary and not sold at a fixed price.
immigration.naturalisation: Ordinarily 10 years of legal residence (reported, with at least 5 as a permanent resident), German at B2, secure income, no criminal record, and a citizenship test. A reform was announced for 2026; its content was not found. From secondary sources and background knowledge, not an official page.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Austria generally requires giving up the previous citizenship, with exceptions (for example descendants of Nazi-persecution victims, or citizenship granted for extraordinary merit in the state's interest). Not verified on an official page.

routes.name: EU/EEA/Swiss free movement
routes.summary: EU citizens register and receive an Anmeldebescheinigung after three months; no permit.
routes.requirements: Directive 2004/38/EC, implemented in the NAG. Non-workers need sufficient funds and health insurance. Permanent residence after 5 years.

routes.name: Settlement permit except gainful employment (Privatier)
routes.summary: Residence for people of independent means who will not work in Austria, subject to a small annual quota.
routes.requirements: Section 44 NAG: a free place in the annual quota (Privatiers: 385 places in the draft 2025 regulation; 2026 figure not found); fixed regular monthly income of at least twice the Ausgleichszulage Richtsatz of Section 293 ASVG (twice EUR 1,308.39 for a single person in 2026, so at least EUR 2,616.78 a month; the number of annual payments used was not confirmed); accommodation, health insurance, no public-funds burden; German language at A1 before the permit under the integration rules (not verified).
routes.physical_presence: Live in Austria; the permit does not allow gainful employment
routes.family: Family reunification possible; quota rules not sourced.
routes.tax_note: Austrian unlimited tax liability follows domicile or habitual abode, not the permit.

routes.summary: Discretionary citizenship for exceptional achievements in art, science, economy or sport that serve the Republic's interest; large investment alone is not enough.
routes.requirements: Government decision (no appeal); achievements must clearly exceed the norm; the grant must be in Austria's interest. Commentators discuss figures from EUR 3 million to 10 million with no fixed price and no guarantee; none is official. Requires no prior residence and may allow keeping the old nationality.
